extraction.name: CT-RATE: A Multimodal Dataset for 3D Chest CT with Radiology Reports
extraction.description: CT-RATE is a public dataset that pairs 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT scans from 21,304 unique patients with corresponding radiology reports. The dataset is designed to support the development of generalist foundation models for 3D medical imaging, enabling tasks such as multi-abnormality detection, case retrieval, and vision-language chat model development.
extraction.license: Open-source (unspecified license, likely CC-BY or similar)

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The CT-RATE dataset was curated from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital, comprising non-contrast chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports acquired between May 2015 and January 2023. The dataset includes 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes from 25,692 distinct CT experiments conducted on 21,304 unique patients. Each scan is accompanied by a radiology report structured into clinical information, technique, findings, and impression sections. The data collection process involved anonymizing patient information, translating reports from Turkish to English, and standardizing CT volumes to ensure consistency.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of 3D chest CT volumes and radiology reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. The CT volumes were reconstructed using various techniques to suit different diagnostic requirements, and the reports were authored by radiologists.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The CT volumes were preprocessed to standardize spacing, resolution, and Hounsfield Unit (HU) values. Specifically, volumes were resized to uniform spacing (0.75 mm in x and y axes, 1.5 mm in z axis), cropped or padded to 480×480×240 resolution, and HU values were clipped to [-1000, 1000] and normalized to [-1, 1]. Metadata was anonymized to remove patient and medical professional identifiers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The preprocessing steps included resizing CT volumes to uniform spacing, cropping or padding to a consistent resolution, converting to Hounsfield Units, clipping and normalizing HU values, and anonymizing metadata. The preprocessing scripts are provided in the dataset's GitHub repository.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-abnormality labels for 18 distinct abnormalities were extracted from radiology reports using an automated text classifier. A subset of 1,000 reports was manually annotated to train the classifier, which was then applied to the remaining reports. The abnormalities were grouped into categories such as medical material, arterial wall calcification, cardiomegaly, pericardial effusion, coronary artery wall calcification, hiatal hernia, lymphadenopathy, emphysema, atelectasis, lung nodule, lung opacity, pulmonary fibrotic sequela, pleural effusion, mosaic attenuation pattern, peribronchial thickening, consolidation, bronchiectasis, and interlobular septal thickening.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The automated label extraction was performed using a finetuned RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m model, which was trained on a subset of manually annotated reports.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The finetuned text encoder achieved high precision, recall, and F1 scores across all abnormalities, indicating robust classification performance. The analysis included evaluating the classifier's performance on a validation set and ensuring the extracted labels were accurate and comprehensive.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is open-source and publicly available via Hugging Face. The maintenance plan includes updates based on user feedback, expansion to include additional modalities and anatomical regions, and integration with other advanced 3D algorithms for improved performance.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes patient demographics such as age and sex, as well as clinical information from radiology reports. However, all patient identifiers have been anonymized to protect privacy.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and associated models aim to improve diagnostic accuracy, reduce radiologist workload, and enhance patient care by enabling the development of advanced AI systems for 3D medical imaging. The models are designed to be clinically relevant and adaptable to diverse patient populations.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is sourced from a single institution, which may introduce biases related to geographic and clinical setting. The dataset includes variability in CT scanners, acquisition protocols, and reconstruction techniques, but the single-center origin may limit generalizability to other populations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to chest CT volumes and does not include other 3D imaging modalities or anatomical regions. The models trained on this dataset may not generalize well to other populations or clinical settings. Additionally, the dataset's single-center origin and the use of specific terminology in reports may introduce biases.
